1	# P15 — token generation at depth: the host term, the stripe, and the split gather
2	
3	**2026-09-22.** Three changes and one measured refusal. A decode step at
4	128 000 cells goes from **22.58 to 27.20 tok/s (1.20x)** and the falloff from
5	depth zero from **0.76x to 0.91x**, with **prefill and depth-zero decode flat
6	as the controls** — 826.5 → 829.4 tok/s at 128k and 29.70 → 29.73 at depth
7	zero, both inside the run-to-run spread.
8	
9	P7–P10 closed the *device's* depth term down to what the attention kernels
10	cost. P14 closed prefill's. What was left was decode's, and it was four terms,
11	one of which was not on the device at all.
12	
13	| depth | pp base | pp final | tg base | tg final |
14	|------:|--------:|---------:|--------:|---------:|
15	| 0 | 1154.4 | 1150.7 | 29.70 | 29.73 |
16	| 8 000 | 972.8 | 969.6 | 28.07 | **28.78** |
17	| 32 000 | 916.2 | 915.3 | 25.87 | **28.72** |
18	| 64 000 | 891.0 | 892.8 | 24.27 | **28.14** |
19	| 128 000 | 826.5 | 829.4 | 22.58 | **27.20** |
20	| falloff | 0.72x | 0.72x | 0.76x | **0.91x** |
21	
22	48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`.
23	**Two passes of the final arm, same hour**, agreeing to 0.2-1.2% on tg
24	(29.73/29.78, 28.78/29.14, 28.72/28.80, 28.14/28.26, 27.20/27.41) and 0.3% on
25	pp (1150.7/1153.7 at depth zero, 829.4/831.8 at 128 000).
26	
27	## Where a 44.3 ms token went
28	
29	The whole of it, and the reason this session went where it did. Per token at
30	128 000 cells, base against final:
31	
32	| term | base | final | Δ |
33	|---|---:|---:|---:|
34	| `attn.attn.split` | 4.109 | 1.571 | **−2.538** |
35	| `attn.score` | 2.533 | 0.995 | **−1.538** |
36	| host `gather` (PLE rows) | 5.175 | 1.263 | **−3.912** |
37	| `attn.select` | 0.862 | 0.862 | — (the control) |
38	| `attn.attn.gather` + `gathmask` | — | 0.249 | +0.249 |
39	| everything else | flat | flat | ~0 |
40	| **a token** | **44.3** | **36.8** | **−7.5** |
41	
42	Every other kernel in the model is flat in depth and was already flat before
43	this: `moe.up` 5.44 → 5.44, `dn.qkv` 4.39 → 4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33 → 2.33. **The
44	depth question in this model is four kernels and one host function**, and it
45	has been since P7.
46	
47	## 1. `PLERows` hashed the whole sequence, every token
48	
49	The largest term in a deep decode step was **on the host**, and it was not
50	attention.
51	
52	`Graph.hidden` gathers the n-gram embedding rows for the tokens it is about to
53	push. It did that by calling `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` — which allocates
54	`len(ids)*NHeads` int32s and hashes **every position in the sequence** — and
55	then slicing off all but the tail:
56	
57	```go
58	rows := PLERows(g.pleCfg, g.ids)[g.past*g.pleCfg.NHeads:]
59	```
60	
61	At 128 000 cells that is 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 million rows hashed, per
62	decode step, to use sixteen of them. Measured: **5.18 ms of a 44.3 ms token,
63	and 3.9 of the 10.6 ms that token gained over one at depth zero.** It was
64	39% of the whole falloff and it never touched the device.
65	
66	`PLERowsFrom(cfg, ids, from)` is the same loop over the tail. The rows are
67	**identical and not merely close, by construction**: a position's row depends
68	on `ids[i-NGram+1 .. i]` and nothing else — the `cut` flag is reset at the top
69	of each position, so no state carries between them — so a suffix that starts
70	far enough back reproduces every row exactly.
71	`TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail` asserts that at *every* cut point of a sequence with
72	an EOS in the middle, which is the one piece of per-position state there is.
73	
74	It is an equality test and not a tolerance one, for `TestPLEGather`'s reason:
75	these are row indices into a 28.80 GB table, so a wrong index is a plausible
76	embedding from somewhere else and nothing downstream would flinch.
77	
78	**The lesson is the profile's shape.** `-depth` had been printing a host
79	`gather` line that went 3.1% → 11.7% between depth zero and 128k for as long as
80	the bench has existed, and every session read past it because the
81	question was always "which kernel". A term that grows 5x with depth is worth
82	looking at whichever side of the bus it is on.
83	
84	## 2. `attn.score` ran on sixteen workgroups of a forty-CU device
85	
86	P9 unpinned the indexer's score from the one workgroup a token it ran on and
87	striped it `attnCellSplits` ways. It set that to 16 and stopped, and nothing
88	since asked whether 16 was the number.
89	
90	It is a **grid and not a reduction** — the kernel's own comment says nothing
91	sums across the stripe, so the tensor it writes is the same bits however the
92	grid is cut — so the only thing that bounds the count is having blocks left to
93	give a workgroup. Measured at decode and 128 000 cells, with
94	`attn.attn.split` flat to 0.4% as the control:
95	
96	| splits | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 |
97	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
98	| `attn.score` µs | 211.6 | 118.5 | **80.9** | 78.5 | 86.5 |
99	
100	64 is the knee; 128 is inside its noise and 256 is past it, where a stripe has
101	too few blocks to pay for its workgroup. It is **better at every depth and not
102	only at the deep end** — 0.126 → 0.106 ms a token at depth zero, 2.533 → 0.995
103	at 128 000 — so there is no crossover to pick a default around, which is why
104	`attnCellSplits` is a constant and not a function of the cache.
105	
106	**1.5 ms a token for a one-line change**, and the reason it was there to find
107	is that P9 was measuring whether the stripe worked at all, not how wide it
108	wanted to be.
109	
110	## 3. The gather and the split compose, and neither had the other's factor
111	
112	This is the change with the argument in it.
113	
114	P14 built the per-cell gather for prefill and wrote down why decode should not
115	take it: *a decode step is 24 single-wave workgroups that all fit at once, so
116	what it costs is one wave's serial walk — which a gather in front of it
117	lengthens rather than cuts.* That is **right about the gather alone** and it is
118	measured here. What it misses is that the two cut different things.
119	
120	Per dispatch at 128 000 cells and one row, four arms, `LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and
121	`LLM_ATTN_GATHER` the knobs:
122	
123	| arm | `attn.attn` µs |
124	|---|---:|
125	| unsplit, block walk | 2948.7 |
126	| unsplit + P13's block list | 2401.1 |
127	| unsplit + gather | 986.7 (+22.4 of gather) |
128	| **split 16, block walk** (shipped) | **419.8** |
129	| **split 16 + gather** (P15) | **129.9** (+21.5 of gather) |
130	
131	The split is **7.12x on the walk**: it cuts how many key blocks one wave has to
132	step through. The gather is **2.99x on the work**: one query row selects 2051
133	cells however deep the cache is, and the block kernel reads every cell of every
134	32-cell block that holds one of them — at 128k that is roughly eight cells
135	visited per cell selected. Neither factor is the other's, and **together they
136	are 3.23x on the shipped kernel** (419.8 → 129.9, two passes agreeing to
137	129.9/129.9 and 420.7/418.9), 2.77x with the gather's own two dispatches
138	charged against it.
139	
140	The gather's cost at decode is the number that decided this, and it was priced
141	*before* anything was built: **22.4 µs against the 419.8 the kernel it feeds
142	was taking**, 5%. A decode tile is one real row and fifteen pad rows, so the
143	"union of sixteen rows" that costs prefill 4.9x over a single row's reach costs
144	decode nothing — the union *is* the row.
145	
146	### What it took
147	
148	`llm_attn_wmma.comp` gains a `GATHER`+`SPLITK` build. Three things had to move:
149	
150	- **`GATHER` is tested before `SPLITK`**, not after. A build can now be both,
151	  and when it is, the axis it walks is the gathered list.
152	- **The list comes in through `cellOff`, not `resOff`.** `resOff` is the
153	  partial arena to every split build and to `llm_attn_combine.comp` behind
154	  them. `cellOff` is the indexer's expanded per-cell score, which P14-1 deleted
155	  and which no attention build has ever read. The push block is full at 64
156	  uints (`TestAttnGPUPushBlockFits`), so a spare field is the whole budget
157	  there is.

content.text:
Everything builds, vets, and the full `llm` suite passes. Here's where it landed.

## What moved

**Token generation at depth — 1.21x at 128k**, with two passes agreeing to 0.2–1.2%:

| depth | tg before | tg after | pp before | pp after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 29.70 | 29.73 | 1154.4 | 1150.7 |
| 8 000 | 28.07 | **28.78** | 972.8 | 969.6 |
| 32 000 | 25.87 | **28.72** | 916.2 | 915.3 |
| 64 000 | 24.27 | **28.14** | 891.0 | 892.8 |
| 128 000 | 22.58 | **27.20** | 826.5 | 829.4 |
| falloff | 0.76x | **0.91x** | 0.72x | 0.72x |

Three changes, all gated, `go test ./llm/` green:

1. **`PLERows` hashed the whole sequence every token** — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows per decode step at 128k, to use sixteen. **5.18 ms of a 44.3 ms token, 39% of the entire falloff, and not on the GPU.** `PLERowsFrom` is exact by construction; `TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail` checks every cut point. The `-depth` profile had been printing this as a host line growing 3.1%→11.7% with depth for as long as the bench has existed.

2. **`attn.score` was striped 16 ways on a 40-CU device.** P9 unpinned it and stopped at 16; the stripe is a grid, not a reduction, so 64 is 2.61x (211.6→80.9 µs) and better at *every* depth. One constant.

3. **The gather and the split compose — P14 said they wouldn't.** That argument is right about the gather *alone* and I measured it (unsplit gather 986.7 µs vs the split's 419.8), but the split cuts the **walk** (7.12x) and the gather cuts the **work** (2.99x). `GATHER`+`SPLITK` together is **3.23x** (419.8 → 129.9 µs). It turns on at `2*selWidth` **live** cells — below that it loses 2.3% — which makes it the first decode knob that moves with depth, so P1c's prerecorded buffer now carries an epoch and re-records the crossing step.

## Two refusals, both measured

- **The arenas' HOST_CACHED type costs the kernels nothing**, even at the 3.85 GB the KV planes now put in that buffer — every kernel within 1% under `LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1` while host glue moves 29x. That was the most plausible remaining explanation for `hc.cn`'s 134 GB/s and for the wide-arena decode cost. Both are now excluded.
- **Allocated-but-unread memory is free**: 3.85 GB of extra `-ctx` costs decode 0.2% (30.23/30.28/30.17 tok/s). So the ubatch's cost is not volume — it's the residency the wide prefill leaves behind. That narrows the open probe.

## What I did *not* move: prompt processing

Prefill is flat here on purpose — it was my control, and it stayed flat (0.3%), which is what makes the decode numbers trustworthy. Prefill was already at `GOALS.md`'s target from P14, and the remaining lever is the ubatch, which I re-priced rather than improved. At `-ctx 139000` the trade is worse than P12-7 found: 4096 buys 1.12x prefill for **0.886x** decode (not 0.92x), and 8192 buys 1.15x for **0.776x**. So 8192 is not a candidate at this depth, and I left `-llm-batch` alone.

The largest depth-scaling term left on the device is now `attn.select` at 0.862 ms a token — the one kernel that can't be striped, and which has never had a two-level histogram-and-merge arrangement. Write-up in `research/p15-decode-at-depth.md`; `TODO.md` updated.
